metadata.note: The Washington Metro (WMATA Metrorail), the DC-area heavy-rail system that opened March 27, 1976 and reached its present extent with the Silver Line's Ashburn extension on November 15, 2022. All six lines are modelled as a sequence of stages with non-overlapping year ranges, so the slider shows the system growing rather than appearing complete in 1976; stages of the same line are the same physical railroad, not parallel routes. Where lines share track (Orange/Blue/Silver through Rosslyn, Yellow/Green through L'Enfant Plaza) the features overlap on the map, as they do in reality. CONVENTION: a stage covers the years in which it held for the majority of the calendar year, so an extension opening in November first appears the following year; every segment note carries the exact opening date. The Green Line ran as two physically disconnected pieces from 1994 to 1999 and is modelled as two features for those years. Geometry is real OSM track; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates, not from a GTFS feed.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Metro (system opened 1976; Blue Line Jul 1 1977; Orange Line Nov 20 1978; Yellow Line Apr 30 1983; Green Line Dec 28 1991; Silver Line Phase 1 Jul 26 2014 -- all five confirmed against the article)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Line_(Washington_Metro) (the 103-mile system was completed by the Green Line extension to Branch Avenue on Jan 13 2001)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhode_Island_Avenue_station and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farragut_North_station (the system opened Mar 27 1976 over 4.6 miles between Rhode Island Avenue and Farragut North, five stations: Rhode Island Avenue, Union Station, Judiciary Square, Gallery Place, Farragut North)
https://ghostsofdc.org/2022/02/22/when-did-metro-open-in-dc/ (Mar 27 1976 opening date and the free first day)

Silver Line Phase 2 to Ashburn opened Nov 15 2022, confirmed against multiple contemporary accounts; individual station-by-station opening dates in the segment notes below have NOT each been checked against a source
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Per-segment verification pass 2026-08-24: 12 of 24 segments now have their opening date verified against a named Wikipedia line article, quoted in the segment's own sources entry. The other 12 turn on dates that are NOT stated in either the Washington Metro article or the relevant line article — Dupont Circle Jan 17 1977, Silver Spring Feb 6 1978, Van Ness–UDC Dec 5 1981, Grosvenor Aug 25 1984, Shady Grove Dec 15 1984, Wheaton Sep 22 1990, Glenmont Jul 25 1998, Van Dorn Street Jun 15 1991, Franconia–Springfield Jun 29 1997, Largo Dec 18 2004, Vienna Jun 7 1986, Huntington Dec 17 1983 and the Sep 18 1999 mid-city connection. Those need a per-station source. Every headway in this file is an estimate.

properties.line: Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority: Metrorail Red Line

segments.note: The first 4.6 miles of Metro opened March 27, 1976: five Red Line stations, Rhode Island Avenue to Farragut North, all inside DC. Gallery Place was added mid-line December 15, 1976.
sources: VERIFIED 2026-08-24: "Service on the Red Line (and the Metro as a whole) began on March 27, 1976, with operation between Farragut North and Rhode Island Avenue." — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Line_(Washington_Metro)
Headway remains an estimate — the opening date is verified, the service frequency is not.

properties.speed_source: estimated; WMATA's system-wide average including station dwells is about 33 mph. Not from a GTFS pull.
properties.geometry_source: Geometry from the OpenStreetMap route relation for each WMATA line (ODbL), fetched through the OSM API and stitched from its member ways, then sliced between the historic terminus stations of each stage using the relation's own station nodes. Douglas-Peucker simplified to ~20 m.
